answer: When an agent stakes an escrow of onyx‑token rewards on an ivory‑signed credential, the network records the stake on a transparent ledge of the consensus ledger. If any downstream node detects a duplicate or inconsistent credential, a timed clawback window of 48 hours triggers automatic redistribution of the full escrow to the verifier, and the offending identity is barred. Thus each fake identity costs the attacker the full escrow amount (e.g., 10 onyx tokens) plus the 48‑hour lock‑up, making large‑scale Sybil attacks financially prohibitive.
